title: Integrated security & compliance playbook: RBAC, audit logging, data residency, SDLC, incident response, evidence workflows
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose

This integrated playbook consolidates Redwood Inference security and compliance operational decisions and procedures spanning RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident-response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and acceptable risk/exception handling. Intended audience: security engineers, SRE, platform engineering, privacy, and compliance reviewers.

Executive summary

- Provide a single reference for operational controls and evidence collection required for customer audits and internal reviews.
- Document owners, guardrails, SLOs, and runbook steps for common compliance scenarios.
- Define threshold-based escalation and exception processes to maintain both agility and auditability.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Overview
- Redwood uses a centralized RBAC model enforced at API gateway, console, and service layers. Roles are mapped to least-privilege permission sets aligned with job functions.
- Primary identity provider (IdP): Okta (SAML/OIDC). Secondary: GitHub OIDC for CI.

Roles and responsibilities
- Role taxonomy: admin, security-admin, infra-operator, runtime-operator, platform-developer, analytics-user, read-only.
- Ownership: Security team maintains role definitions and approval flows. Team leads request role assignments through Access Request workflow.

Access request & approval procedure (numbered steps)
1. Requester files access request in Access Requests Confluence template and attaches business justification and expiry.
2. Team lead performs peer review and approves in the Okta request ticket (T+2 business days target).
3. Security performs risk check for high-privilege roles (security-admin, admin).
4. Approved requests are provisioned via SCIM into Okta and propagated to service-level IAM (internal RBAC engine).

Enforcement & technical controls
- All service-to-service authentication uses short-lived mTLS certificates issued by internal CA (rotation every 30 days).
- User authentication enforces MFA for interactive users and conditional access for privileged roles (geofencing, device posture).
- Access tokens: OIDC tokens with 1 hour lifetime; refresh tokens not issued for machine accounts.
- Privileged commands in consoles require just-in-time (JIT) elevation audited with an approval record.

SLOs and audit thresholds
- Time-to-provision (standard roles): <= 2 business days for 95% of requests.
- Privileged role approval (security review): <= 3 business days.
- Monthly privilege recertification reminder: automated email 30 days before entitlement expiry.

2) Audit logging & monitoring

Scope
- Audit logging captures user logins, privilege elevations, API requests (create/update/delete), configuration changes, model deploys/rollbacks, and data access events.

Log collection & retention
- Primary log aggregation: ELK stack (Elastic) in dedicated security cluster with WORM storage for evidence retention.
- Retention policy table:
| Event class | Retention (internal) | Retention (customer-facing evidence) | Rationale |
|-------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| Auth & access events | 2 years | 2 years | Required for security investigations and customer audits |
| Config changes (infra) | 1 year | 1 year | Operational troubleshooting |
| Model deploy audit trail | 3 years | 1 year | Model lineage and compliance |
| Data access / exfiltration alerts | 5 years | 5 years | For high-sensitivity customers / e-discovery |

Log integrity & access controls
- All logs are signed and ingested with SHA-256 checksums and stored on immutable S3 with access restricted by IAM policy.
- Read access to audit logs requires security approval and is logged (every access creates an audit record).

Alerting & runbooks
- Key alerts: repeated failed authentication (>10 in 5 minutes), sudden privilege escalations, mass data download (>100GB in 1 hour), anomalous model output pattern detection.
- For each alert class the incident response runbook (section 5) must be followed. Thresholds and tuning are reviewed quarterly.

3) Data residency & retention

Policy summary
- Customer data is stored in region-specific clusters per account configuration. Default regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1 (by request).
- Customers can select residency-only deployments (no cross-region replication) for regulated workloads.

Data classification & handling
- Data classes: public, internal, sensitive, regulated (PII/PHI). Handling rules: encryption at rest (AES-256), in transit (TLS 1.3), and access limited by RBAC.

Retention and deletion workflows (step-by-step)
1. Data created by customer (user inputs, logs for that tenant) are retained according to the account-level retention setting (default 90 days).
2. Data deletion request: Customer support raises a deletion ticket, security reviews for legal holds, and engineers perform deletion from primary and backup stores within SLA.
3. Evidence of deletion (deletion manifest) is created and signed; delivered to customer as part of compliance package.

Cross-border transfers & controls
- Any replication to a secondary region requires customer opt-in and explicit documented consent stored in the account record.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle) controls

Standards & gates
- All code merges to main require: passing CI pipeline (unit tests, linting), Snyk vulnerability scan (no critical/high unresolved), and peer review (2 approvers for infra/runtime changes).
- Security-critical changes (auth, RBAC, data handling) require a Security Design Review (SDR) with security engineer sign-off.

Developer tooling & automation
- CI uses ephemeral runners with short-lived OIDC tokens; secrets retrieved from Vault via workload identity.
- Dependency policy: auto-bot for dependency updates; security team triages transitive vulnerabilities weekly.

Release and deployment controls
- Canary rollout for runtime and model-serving changes with automated rollback on error budget burn (error budget policy in eng-sre runbook).
- Production deploy checklist (table):
| Item | Owner | Required evidence |
|------|-------|-------------------|
| Unit & integration tests | Author | CI status link |
| Vulnerability scan | DevSec | Snyk report link |
| Load/perf baseline | SRE | Perf-run report |
| Security design review | Security | SDR ticket id |

5) Incident response — security procedures

Notification & triage
- All security incidents must follow the standard incident process but with security lead included in the first 30 minutes.
- Severity matrix (high level):
  - Sev 1: confirmed data exfiltration, production compromise, or cryptographic key compromise
  - Sev 2: suspected privilege abuse, persistent unauthorized access, or major availability impact
  - Sev 3: localized failures, non-production incidents, low-impact alerts

Immediate steps (first 60 minutes)
1. Triage call initiated (Slack incident channel + Zoom bridge).
2. Capture scope: affected systems, user accounts, potential data exfiltrated, and attack vector.
3. Apply containment: revoke affected tokens, block suspicious IPs, or isolate compromised hosts.
4. Notify Legal and Privacy if data exposure is possible.

Investigation & evidence preservation
- Preserve volatile evidence per forensics checklist: snapshots of memory (if available), filesystem images, logs copies, and network captures.
- Chain-of-custody: all evidence collection is recorded in Audit Evidence Tracker with signer and timestamp.

Communication & regulatory reporting
- Public/customer notification thresholds defined: any confirmed customer data leak requires notification within contractual timelines (see contracts-and-legal page for SLA specifics).
- For regulated incidents (GDPR/UK DPA/HIPAA), Legal leads the external notification; Security provides a technical timeline and remediation plan.

Post-incident review and remediation
- Postmortem required for Sev 1/2 with security action items prioritized into the roadmap. Remediation verification includes regression tests and targeted audits.

6) Compliance evidence workflows & packaging

Evidence types and sources
- Identity & access: Okta activity reports, role assignment logs, SCIM provisioning logs.
- Audit logs: Elastic snapshots, immutable S3 manifests.
- Change control: Git commit history, PR approvals, CI run artifacts.
- SDLC artifacts: Snyk reports, SDR sign-off docs, test coverage reports.

Packaging process (steps)
1. Compliance request received (customer or auditor) with scope and time window.
2. Security analyst creates an Evidence Package workspace and lists required artifacts.
3. Collect artifacts from sources, verify checksums and signatures, and place into a read-only evidence bucket.
4. Generate evidence index (manifest) with timestamps and originating system IDs.

Delivery options
- Secure share (temporary S3 pre-signed URL with password protection), remote auditor access to read-only console, or full package export (signed tarball). All deliveries require Legal approval for sensitive customers.

7) Risk exceptions & documented compensating controls

Exception request lifecycle
1. Request submitted with risk justification, mitigation plan, and expiry date.
2. Security reviews and assigns a residual risk rating (low/medium/high).
3. Exceptions with high residual risk require CISO approval and quarterly reviews.

Compensating controls examples
- If a legacy service cannot support short-lived credentials, require network segmentation + traffic monitoring + additional log retention for that service.
- Where encryption at rest is not available for a specific datastore, require application-layer encryption and limited admin access.

Exception register & reporting
- All granted exceptions are recorded in the Risk Exceptions ledger (quarterly export) and reviewed by the Audit & Risk Committee.

C. Quarterly review checklist
- Review RBAC roles and remove stale privileges (Owner: team leads)
- Validate retention policy alignment with top 10 customers (Owner: privacy)
- Run synthetic SIEM alert scenarios and tune thresholds (Owner: security ops)
